The Big Beautiful Bill's Medicaid cuts expose Washington's real priority: protecting pharmaceutical middlemen and hospital billing consultants who profit from bloated administration. Section 44142's $35 co-pays for low-income patients will create medical debt while doing nothing to rein in $200B in annual Medicaid overpayments to insurers.

The bill fails to implement block grants that could save $500B by cutting red tape, not care. Rural hospitals are already collapsing under 8.5% administrative overhead costs - this legislation doubles down on the same failed payment models.

Real reform would follow the Texas model of Medicaid fraud recovery, which clawed back $6B from corrupt providers last year alone. Until Congress stops letting insurers and hospital chains write the rules, these "cuts" will just shuffle money between bureaucratic pockets.
